cost: THE THREE SUBJECTS LAND 65 / 56 / 53 AGAINST STATED 60 / 52 / 50, AND THE WALL IS ONE OF HIS OWN PINS. Dorian Finney-Smith '20 is pinned 55 +-3 by recal_118 and already reads its bottom edge; he is 29.9 minutes, 13.0% usage, orb 78, a standard path of 41.01 under a floor of 59.80, which makes him the SAME CARD as Maxi Kleber '20 on every bar this term reads except minutes. At the shipped line he reads 51.517 of raw against a band edge of 51.500 — the admissible window's top is about 31.62 and the measured quartile 31.60 sits inside it with two hundredths of a point to spare. At recal_163's existing SECOND_FULL of 33.9 the subjects read 64 / 55 / 52 — closer to his numbers on ALL THREE — and Finney-Smith reads 50, two outside his pin. A later round that wants 60 / 52 / 50 is asking for that pin to be released, exactly as recal_170 asked for the Lakers rank.

THE SECOND WALL IS recal_170's OWN BENCH PIN AND IT FIXES THE RAMP'S FOOT. Donyell Marshall '07 (16.8 mpg) is pinned 52 +-3 and now reads 49, the bottom edge. Raising the foot above recal_96's 12 is what a steeper ramp needs — the optimum with both walls binding is a foot near 13 and a top near 31.5 — and it buys the subject nothing: Anderson reads 65 anywhere in that whole family. 65 is therefore the FLOOR of what is reachable with every pin held, not a choice of constant.

THE SCORING-LOAD READING THE SCAN ASKED FOR IS PROVABLY INFEASIBLE, MEASURED IN EVERY FORM. `usg_raw x load` (recal_169's shape), `usg_raw x mpg` (the same count without the 24-minute saturation), raw usage, and recal_112's volume ramp were each solved against the standing pins. Two pairs close the door in opposite directions: Finney-Smith '20 (13.0% usage) must KEEP 91% of his correction while Kleber '20 (13.2%) must lose half of it, and OG Anunoby '21 (18.5% usage, pinned 65 +-2 and reading 63 with ZERO room down) sits ABOVE Mo Bamba '22 (17.2%), who must fall four. No factor monotone in scoring load can separate either pair. MINUTES is the one axis that orders the board the way his own rulings do, and it is the axis recal_170 already put on this line.

With ONE line across both branches Tony Snell '18 falls 50 -> 48 and leaves recal_64's 50 +-1; Korver '15, Kerr '96 and Bowen '06 hold either way. The wing class's own second-payment quartile was not measured here, so the wing floor keeps recal_96's 24-minute line and every non-big card on the board is byte-identical.

WHY THE LINE IS A SECOND LINE, AND IT IS recal_130's DOCTRINE APPLIED WHERE IT HAD NOT BEEN. recal_170 paid this correction at recal_96's load share, whose full-load line is 24 minutes — a line located by Clint Capela '17 at 23.9 and cut to ask 'did this man play at all'. 493 of the 1,083 bigs this floor binds on sat at share 1.0000, from a 24-minute bench big to a 40-minute starter, and the floor is worth up to twenty-four printed OFF points. recal_91's three added terms are bars the STANDARD PATH ALREADY PAYS EVERY CARD — orb at 0.06, rim inside the zone block at 0.22/0.08/0.05, volume at 0.26 x load_share — so this branch is a second payment in recal_130's exact sense: 'a rate paid twice has to be scaled twice, and the second line is not the bench boundary'. recal_163 set its own second line the same way (SECOND_FULL 33.9, the upper quartile of minutes among the 193 cards its two terms pay).

THE CONSTANT IS MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN, AND THE ALTERNATIVES ARE ON THE RECORD. The class is the cards this floor binds on inside recal_91's branch (1,083 bigs; minutes p25 19.7, median 23.2, p75 28.2, p90 31.76). The line is measured on the sub-class the OLD line could not tell apart — the 493 that recal_96's 24-minute line paid IN FULL — whose upper quartile of minutes is 31.60 (p25 26.1, median 28.7). Measured alternatives, all on the full pipeline: 28.2 (the whole binding class's quartile) reads Anderson 66 and reaches nobody; 30.1 (the quartile of the 2,880 cards inside the branch's gate) reads him 66; 31.76 (the binding class's upper decile) and 33.9 (recal_163's existing line) both take Dorian Finney-Smith '20 out of recal_118's band. Every line from about 30.7 to 31.62 reads the subjects 65 / 56 / 53-54 and holds all 187 pins.

MEASURED BEFORE APPLYING, on the whole pool. 353 of 10,000 cards move on OFF, EVERY ONE OF THEM DOWN (a share can only discount a correction; there are ZERO rises), max -5, mean -1.85. OVR follows on 254, max -4. DEF moves on ZERO cards and no attribute moves at all — this is a compute_ovr-only round. The top 12 by OFF is identical name for name and the top 50 by OVR has no entrant, no leaver and no rank flip. Nothing at 31.6 minutes or above moves by a thousandth.
